subject: Orchid Therapeutics — cross-border DPF mapping & SCCs alternative Q/A
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@orchidtx.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidtx.com, legal@orchidtx.com
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Initial DPF mapping request and SCCs alternatives

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — Orchid is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Procurement and legal have a couple of asks before we move to contract: a cross-border data processing framework (DPF) mapping populated for our use case, and whether Redwood can accept the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or provide an equivalent transfer mechanism.

Attached is our DPF template (we call it the "DPF mapping workbook") — can you confirm which fields you can populate and what evidence you can provide (logs, architecture diagrams, KMS control points)? Procurement has a tight timeline: they want a completed workbook and any redline comments by EOD Nov 7.

Quick questions for you:
- Do you offer SCCs as a toggle, or do you require a DPA annex?
- For customers requiring EU→US transfers only, what operational safeguards do you typically document (e.g., encryption in transit+at rest, access controls, subprocessor list, key custody)?

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Park
Head of Privacy & Security
Orchid Therapeutics

[Attachment: Orchid_DPF_Template_v2.xlsx]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@orchidtx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 11:07:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPF mapping request and SCCs alternatives

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask and the workbook. Looping in Karthik (technical privacy) and Marissa (legal & evidence). We'll start populating the workbook today and aim to deliver a draft by Nov 5 so you have time for review before EOD Nov 7.

High-level answers now:
- SCCs: Redwood supports execution of the standard EU SCCs in our DPA annex. We can also accept a customer's redlines in most cases; we route redlines through legal for review.
- Mechanism: For EU→US transfers we commonly rely on SCCs + technical and organizational safeguards; for some regulated customers we offer a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) as an alternative to relying on SCCs.

We will include: a filled DPF mapping worksheet, a redline-friendly DPA annex PDF (with trackable comments), and an evidence pack (architecture diagram, KMS controls summary, sample audit log snippet). If you have preferred formats for evidence (CSV for logs, PNG for diagrams) let us know.

Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_response_plan.txt]

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 08:23:00 -05:00
Subject: Internal: DPF mapping approach for Orchid

Connor — draft notes from the infra/privacy side for the workbook population:

What we can populate (per column names in their template):
- Data categories: copy, confirm as "customer PII/PHI tokens" where applicable.
- Legal basis: processor operations — will default to "performance of contract" / processing on behalf of controller.
- Transfer mechanism: SCCs (executed via DPA annex) — include fallback to private deployment for regulated data.
- Data flow: will include sequence: customer app -> Redwood API (hosted) -> Dedicated inference workers (if enabled) -> optional cold storage (S3) for logs/aggregates.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest with customer KMS option for Dedicated/Private.
- Access controls: RBAC, SIEM alerts, periodic access reviews, contractually limited support access.
- Subprocessors: provide current list + 30d notice.

Outstanding items for legal to confirm:
1) We should include sample retention windows per data category.
2) Evidence: we can provide a redacted log sample showing request IDs+timestamps; need to validate redaction policy for Orchid.
3) Key custody: we have two modes — Redwood-managed keys (default) and customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private customers.

I'll prepare the DPF workbook draft and a short architecture PNG.

-Karthik
VP, Applied Privacy Engineering

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@orchidtx.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, legal@orchidtx.com
Date: Mon, 06 Nov 2028 10:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Redwood DPA annex and SCCs redline (initial)

Julia — attaching our proposal: an editable DPA annex with SCCs executed as an exhibit, plus a redline.pdf that highlights the few non-standard clauses we typically push back on (primarily around liability and subprocessor notice windows). Key points:

- We can execute the EU SCCs as-is; if Orchid requires alternate transfer mechanisms we can present our private deployment offering with separate SOW/pricing.
- Retention: default request logs retained for 90 days; customers can configure longer retention on Dedicated/Private (90/365/730 options).
- Evidence: enclosed architecture diagram and a redacted log sample (sample only; production logs require DSAR process).

Requested action: please confirm which fields in the workbook you would like Redwood to populate vs. which you prefer to fill. If legal wants to propose specific DPA redlines, send those back in PDF so we can provide a tracked response.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

[Attachments: SCCs_redline_Orchid.pdf, Redwood_architecture_overview.png, redaction_example.txt]

From: Julia Park <julia.park@orchidtx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidtx.com, legal@orchidtx.com, connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 07 Nov 2028 09:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA annex and SCCs redline (initial)

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Team asked that Redwood populate the following tabs in our workbook: Data Categories, Data Flows, Transfer Mechanism, and Technical Safeguards. We will fill controller business details and retention policy columns after your input.

A few clarifying asks from Orchid legal:
1) Can you confirm whether key rotation events are logged and exposed in a way customers can audit? If yes, what fields are present in those logs?
2) For the redaction sample: please confirm the redaction tool/process and provide a short description for our audit (one-paragraph).

Procurement echoes the Nov 7 timeline — please send the populated workbook and redline PDF by EOD today if possible.

Julia

From: connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@orchidtx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 07 Nov 2028 17:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Final: Populated DPF workbook + SCCs redline

Julia — attached deliverables (zip contains: Orchid_DPF_Template_populated.xlsx, SCCs_redline_Orchid.pdf with comments, redacted_log_sample.csv, architecture_overview.png). Summary of changes and answers to your two legal questions:

1) Key rotation logging: Yes. Key rotation events are recorded in our KMS audit logs with the following fields: event_timestamp, key_id (masked), rotation_type, initiating_principal, rotation_status. We can provide a redacted excerpt; full KMS logs are available to customers in Dedicated/Private deployments via integration with customer SIEM and their KMS (subject to contractual access).

2) Redaction process: Redaction is performed by our internal compliance tooling which strips or tokenizes PII fields and replaces values with deterministic placeholders. The redaction tool records schema fields redacted and redaction method (mask/tokenize). We included a one-paragraph description and the redaction_example.txt attachment.

Next steps we propose:
- Please review the populated workbook and call out any cells needing further specificity.
- If Orchid wants changes to the SCCs, send back the redline and we will respond line-by-line; otherwise we can provide an executed DPA with SCC exhibit on signature.

Deliverables (attached): Orchid_DPF_Template_populated.xlsx; SCCs_redline_Orchid.pdf; redacted_log_sample.csv; architecture_overview.png

Best,
Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

[Attachments: Orchid_DPF_Template_populated.xlsx, SCCs_redline_Orchid.pdf, redacted_log_sample.csv, architecture_overview.png]
